advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test injecting a non-LockTimeout exception (e.g. StoreError/generic Exception) on append_event/write_and_push and assert emit returns False after exactly ONE attempt (calls['n'] == 1), proving the discriminator does not retry non-contention errors.
evidence: src/rebar/llm/completion_sidecar.py:53-63: `_is_lock_timeout_error` distinguishes retryable LockTimeout (raw or `returncode==1 and str(exc).startswith('flock:')`) from all other errors

ABSENCE: all three emit-level tests (test_pass_sidecar_retries_raw_lock_timeout_and_lands, test_pass_sidecar_retries_lock_boundary_timeout_and_lands, test_pass_sidecar_permanent_lock_timeout_returns_false) inject only LockTimeout; none injects a non-lock exception to assert single-attempt propagation to False
advisory.finding: No test covers the non-LockTimeout exception branch of _append_sidecar_retrying (`if not _is_lock_timeout_error(exc): raise`). The fix's discriminator retries ONLY LockTimeout (raw or CommandError-wrapped) and must propagate any other error immediately without a retry, ultimately returning False from emit. A regression that broadened the retry to all exceptions, or that mis-classified errors, would not be caught: the tests exercise raw-LockTimeout-retried, wrapped-LockTimeout-retried, and permanent-LockTimeout, but never a distinct non-lock failure (e.g. a StoreError / generic Exception) to prove it is NOT retried and surfaces as False on the first attempt.
scenarios: A future refactor that removes/broadens the _is_lock_timeout_error guard so every exception is retried once — no test would fail
A non-transient store error being erroneously retried, doubling wasted work under a permanent fault
advisory.suggested_fix: Add: def test_pass_sidecar_non_lock_error_not_retried(store, monkeypatch): monkeypatch event_append.write_and_push (or _seam.append_event) to raise a generic Exception, count calls, assert emit(...) is False and calls['n'] == 1 (no retry) and latest_pass_record is None.
